questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer has 200 windings in the primary and 400 windings in the secondary. The primary is connected to an AC supply of 110 V and a current of 10 A flows in it. The voltage across the secondary and the current in it, respectively, are
questions.solution:
Voltage across secondary coil is
$E_s=E_\rho \times \frac{N_s}{N_p}=\frac{110 \times 400}{200}=220 \mathrm{ V}$
Current in secondary coil is
$I_s=I_p \times \frac{E_p}{E_s}=\frac{10 \times 110}{220}=5 \mathrm{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The primary of a transformer has 400 turns while the secondary has 2000 turns. If the power output from the secondary at 1000 V is 12 kW. The resistance of the primary is $0.2 \Omega$ and that of the secondary is $2 \Omega$. If the efficiency of the transformer is $80 \%$, then the power loss in the primary is
questions.solution:
$N_p=400, \mathrm{N_s}=2000$ and $E_s=1000 \mathrm{ V}$
Now, $\frac{E_p}{E_s}=\frac{N_p}{N_s}$ or $\quad E_p=\frac{E_s \times N_p}{N_s}=\frac{1000 \times 400}{2000}=200 \mathrm{ V}$
Since the efficiency is $80 \%$, the input power is
$12 \mathrm{ kW} \times \frac{100}{80}=15 \mathrm{ kW}\therefore$ Current in the primary is
$\begin{aligned} I_p & =\frac{\text{ Input power }}{\text{ Input voltage }}=\frac{15 \mathrm{ kW}}{200 \mathrm{ V}} \\ & =\frac{15 \times 1000}{200}=75 \mathrm{ A}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Power loss in primary $=I_\rho^2 R_\rho=(75)^2 \times 0.2\begin{aligned} & =1125 \mathrm{ W}=1.125 \mathrm{ kW} \\ & =1125 \mathrm{ W}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In A.C. circuit in which inductance and capacitance are joined in series. Current is found to be maximum when the value of inductance is \(0.5 $\mathrm{H}$\) and the value of capacitance is \(8 \mu $\mathrm{F}$\). The angular frequency of applied alternating voltage will be:
questions.solution:
Current is max, when at resonance condition
So, $\omega=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{LC}}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{0.5 \times 8 \times 10^{-6}}}\)
\begin{aligned}& \omega=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4 \times 10^{-6}}}\\
& \omega=\frac{1 \times 1000}{2}\\
& \omega=500 \mathrm{ Hz}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two coils have a mutual inductance $0.005 \mathrm{H}$. The current changes in the first coil according to equation $\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_{0} \sin \omega \mathrm{t}$, where $\mathrm{I}_{0}=10 \mathrm{ A}$ and $\omega=100 \pi$ radian $/ \mathrm\sec$. The maximum value of e.m.f. in the second coil is
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \mathrm{e}$&=$\mathrm{M} \frac{\mathrm{di}}{\mathrm{dt}}=0.005 \times \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}} \left(\mathrm{I}_{0} \sin \omega \mathrm{t}\right)\\ \text{ and } =0.0005 \times \mathrm{I}_{0} \omega \cos \omega \mathrm{t}\\ \therefore \mathrm{e}_{\max }$&=0.005 \times10 \times100 $\pi=5 \pi \quad[\because \cos \omega \mathrm{t}=1] \end{aligned} \end{array}$

questions.q: Resonance frequency of LCR series a.c. circuit is $\mathrm{f}_{0}$. Now the capacitance is made 4 times, then the new resonance frequency will become
questions.solution: In LCR series circuit, resonance frequency $\mathrm{f}_{0}$ is given by $\begin{array}{c} L \omega=\frac{1}{\mathrm{C} \omega} \Rightarrow \omega^{2}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{LC}} \quad \therefore \quad \omega=\sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{LC}}}=2 \pi \mathrm{f}_{0}\\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{f}_{0}=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{\mathrm{LC}}} \quad \text{ or } \quad \mathrm{f}_{0} \alpha \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{C}}} \end{array}$ When the capacitance of the circuit is made 4 times, its resonant frequency become $\mathrm{f}_{0}^{\prime} \therefore \frac{\mathrm{f}_{0}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{f}_{0}}=\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{C}}}{\sqrt{4 \mathrm{C}}} \quad \text{ or } \quad \mathrm{f}_{0}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{f}_{0}}{2}$

questions.q: If $i_{1}=3 \sin \omega t$ and $i_{2}=4 \cos \omega t$, then $i_{3}$ is
questions.solution: $From Kirchhoff's current law, \begin{array}{l} i_{3}=i_{1}+i_{2}=3 \sin \omega t+4 \sin\left(\omega t+90^{{}^{\circ}}\right) \\ =\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}+2(3)(4) \cos 90^{{}^{\circ}}} \sin(\omega t+\phi) \\ \text{ where } \tan \phi=\frac{4 \sin 90^{{}^{\circ}}}{3+4 \cos 90^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{4}{3} \\ \therefore i_{3}=5 \sin\left(\omega t+53^{{}^{\circ}}\right) \end{array}$

questions.solution:
Maximum current flows in the circuit in resonance condition Current in the LCR circuit
$i=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+\left(X_{L}-X_{C}\right)^{2}}}$
For current to be maximum denominator should be minimum $\left(X_{L}-X_{C}\right)^{2}=0\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}} \Rightarrow \omega \mathrm{L}=\frac{1}{\omega \mathrm{C}} \\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{L}=\frac{1}{\omega^{2} \mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{(100)^{2} \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} \\
\quad \mathrm{~L}=\frac{1}{10} \mathrm{H}=0.1 \mathrm{H}=100 \mathrm{mH}
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In an A.C. circuit resistance \(R\), inductance \(L\) and capacitance \(C\) are in parallel. The value of \(R\) is \(50 \Omega\), inductive reactance $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=40 \Omega\) and capacitive reactance \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=25 \Omega\). Then the reading of ammeter will be:
$
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
& $\mathrm{I}=\sqrt{\mathrm{I}^2{ }_{\mathrm{R}}+\left(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{C}}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{L}}\right)^2}$\\
& $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{200}{50}=$4 $\mathrm{~A}$\\
& $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\frac{200}{25}=$8 $\mathrm{~A}$\\
& $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}}=\frac{200}{40}=$5 $\mathrm{~A}$\\
& $\mathrm{I}=\sqrt{(4)^2+(8-5)^2}$\\
& $\mathrm{I}=\sqrt{16+9}=\sqrt{25}$\\
& $\mathrm{I}=$5 $\mathrm{~A}
\end{aligned}$\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What direct current will produce the same amount of thermal energy in a resistance \(R=\) \(2 \Omega\) as an alternating current that a peak value of \(4.24 $\mathrm{ A}$\) and frequency \(50 $\mathrm{ Hz}$\) ?
questions.solution:
Peak current, \($\mathrm{I}}_{0}=4.24  \mathrm{~A}\)
\(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{\sqrt{2}}=  \left(\frac{4.24}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\)
Thermal energy produced,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{H}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}^$2  $\mathrm{RT}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}^$2 $\mathrm{RT}\\
& \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}^2}
\end{aligned}\)
Direct current,
\$(I_d=\sqrt{\left(\frac{4.24}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}=\frac{4.24}{\sqrt{2}}=$2.99  $\mathrm{~A} \simeq$3  $\mathrm{~A}$\)

options: frequency of AC supply is increased
